context.title: Application context
context.description: Background about the application that every agent receives before its own instructions. It cannot override the assistant's fixed rules. Do not include personal data or secrets.
context.label: Context text

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: Code agents come from the application; you can override or reset them. Agents you create here can be deleted. Pause, stop and resume any agent; its definition stays as it is.
agents.reset-keeps-state: Resetting restores the code definition; the agent stays active, paused or stopped as it is.

state.configured-off-hint: Disabled in the application's code until the next deployment; it cannot be resumed here.
state.off-hint: Events, schedules and other triggers are ignored until it is switched on, and nothing waits for it. People can still chat with it and start it by hand.
state.starts-off: It started off, as its code says.
state.stopped-was-off-hint: It was off when it stopped: releasing the kill switch switches it back off. Resume switches it on.
state.stopped-was-on-hint: It was not off when it stopped: releasing the kill switch makes it work again, as Resume does.

explain.active: The agent works again. Every subject with waiting events gets one run.
explain.paused: No new runs start. Events wait and run after the resume; running work finishes and approved proposals execute.
explain.off: Events, schedules, webhooks, hand-offs and follow-ups are ignored and nothing waits; switching on later starts nothing for them. Running work finishes, open proposals can still be decided and people can still chat with the agent and start it by hand.
explain.switch-on: The agent takes its events, schedules and other triggers again. Nothing that happened while it was off runs.
explain.stopped: Active runs are cancelled, their open proposals withdrawn and waiting events dropped. Approved proposals wait until the agent works again.

state.note-hint: Shown on this agent with your name and the time until the next change. The agent does not read it.

skills.title: Skills
skills.budget: Budget per day: {{calls}} tool calls, {{tokens}} tokens

explain.active: The skill {{skill}} works again. Every subject with events waiting for it gets one run.
explain.paused: The skill {{skill}} starts no new runs: its events wait, triage no longer chooses it and running work finishes. The other skills keep working.
explain.off: Triggers of the skill {{skill}} are ignored and rules and triage no longer route work to it; nothing waits for it. Running work finishes. The other skills keep working.
explain.switch-on: The skill {{skill}} takes work again. Nothing that happened while it was off runs.
explain.stopped: The runs of the skill {{skill}} are cancelled and its waiting events dropped; its triggers are refused. The other skills keep working.

shadow.hint: Its work goes to shadow threads that only administrators see.
shadow.locked: A shadow variant always works in shadow.

explain.shadow: New runs work in shadow threads that only administrators see: nobody is notified and nothing proposed there executes. Running work finishes as it started; the live threads and their open proposals stay.
explain.live: New runs work live: people see them, are notified and decide their proposals.
explain.code: The mode in code decides again.
explain.own: The agent's own setting decides again: {{mode}}.

skill-explain.shadow: Work that reaches the skill {{skill}} goes to the shadow threads; the other skills keep their mode.
skill-explain.live: The skill {{skill}} works live again, unless its agent works in shadow.
skill-explain.code: The mode in code decides again for the skill {{skill}}.
skill-explain.own: The own setting of the skill {{skill}} decides again: {{mode}}.

explain.set: New runs answer to this account and use its rights. Runs that started and their proposals keep their account.
explain.code: New runs answer to the account in code again: {{account}}.

consultation-routes.title: Consultation routes
consultation-routes.description: Switch a route off for all consultations of this agent at once, in code and in the administration. When another assistant consults this agent and the agent proposes a change, a route decides who decides it and whose rights run it.
consultation-routes.load-failed: The consultation routes could not be read.

explain.asker-decides: The person who asked decides in their own chat; it runs with their own rights.
explain.subject-agent-rights: The subject's approvers other than the person who asked decide; it runs with the agent's own rights.
explain.subject-asker-rights: The subject's approvers decide; it runs later with the rights of the person who asked.

consultation-routes.not-allowed-hint: No consultation of this agent allows this route, so it stays off and cannot be switched on.

action.code: Back to what the consultations allow

explain-change.on: Consultations use this route for new proposals again. Proposals already recorded keep their route.
explain-change.off: Consultations no longer use this route for new proposals; with every route off, the agent's consultations only read. Proposals already recorded keep their route.
explain-change.code-on: The consultations decide again: one of them allows this route, so it is on.
explain-change.code-off: The consultations decide again: none of them allows this route, so it stays off.

works-on.label: Works on:
works-on.run-policy: Run for the whole application by: {{policy}}.
works-on.view-policy: Results for the whole application seen by: {{policy}}.

agents.catalog-failed: The building blocks of agent runs could not be read. Until they are, agents cannot be run now here and what an agent works on and its groups stay as they are.

warnings.classification-not-permitted: Neither the agent's model profile nor the profile's fallbacks permit its data classification. The agent is saved, but its model calls are refused until a profile permits the classification.

agent-editor.id-hint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. The id cannot change later.
agent-editor.instructions-hint: What the agent does and how it answers.
agent-editor.autonomy-hint: Only Execute allows changes in the agent's own work. In a consultation that may propose, Propose and Simulate propose changes too. Every change still needs approval.
agent-editor.required-policy-hint: Optional. Only users who pass this policy see the agent.
agent-editor.profile-hint: The model the agent works with, from the profiles the application offers for agents created here.
agent-editor.classification-hint: How sensitive the data is that the agent's model calls carry, in chats with it and in its runs. Its model profile or one of the profile's fallbacks must permit it; a skill may set its own.
agent-editor.state-hint: Pause, stop and resume the agent from the agent list. Saving never changes its state.
agent-editor.switch-on-now-hint: Otherwise the agent starts off: its events, schedules and other triggers are ignored until you switch it on in the agent list. People can still chat with it and start it by hand.
agent-editor.tool-selectors-hint: Choose tools from the catalog or add a pattern such as sample-api.project.*. MCP tools come from the assigned servers.
agent-editor.no-selectors: No tool selectors. The agent can only answer from its instructions and assigned MCP servers.
agent-editor.mcp-servers-hint: Enabled tools of these servers become available to this agent.

use.title: How is this agent used?
use.chat-hint: People choose it in the assistant to ask questions and get work done.
use.background-hint: It starts on events or a schedule and proposes work; it is not offered in the chat.
use.both-hint: Offered in the chat, and it also starts on events or a schedule.
use.next: After saving, a short setup asks when the agent starts, what it does and on whose behalf.

works-on.title: What does this agent work on?
works-on.hint: Events, schedules, people and other agents start it only on what it works on.
works-on.all-hint: Every kind of object the application has, now and later.
works-on.types-hint: Only the kinds of objects you tick below.
works-on.no-types: The application has no kinds of objects to choose from.
works-on.too-many: Choose at most 20 kinds of objects, or All objects.
works-on.application-hint: Work that concerns no single object, such as a weekly overview.
works-on.per-division-hint: Its work for the whole application, such as its schedules, runs separately for every division.
works-on.missing: Choose at least one kind of object, or the whole application.
works-on.run-policy: Who may run it for the whole application
works-on.run-policy-hint: People who pass this may start the agent for the whole application.
works-on.view-policy: Who sees its results for the whole application
works-on.view-policy-default: Everyone who may use the agent (default)
works-on.view-policy-hint: Results on an object follow who may read that object.

groups.title: Groups
groups.hint: Pages of the application show the agents of a group on a board, with their latest results. Your choice wins over the code.
groups.shadow-variant: A shadow variant works for administrators only and joins no group.

metadata.title: Application fields
metadata.hint: The application keeps its own data about agents here. Each field has an editor of the application, which saves it on its own.
metadata.save-first: Save the agent first; then its fields appear here.
metadata.load-failed: The fields of this agent could not be loaded.
metadata.no-editor: The application shows no editor for this field.
metadata.read-only: Set in the application's code; it cannot change here.

source.override: Changed here, over the value in code

agent-editor.catalog-unavailable: The building blocks of agent runs could not be read, so what this agent works on and its groups cannot be changed now. Saving keeps them as they are.

mcp.title: MCP servers
mcp.description: Connect remote MCP servers. Their tools start disabled and are treated as changes that need approval until you mark them read-only.

headless.personal: Background runs with the person's own account, after consent

transport.auto: Streamable HTTP with fallback to HTTP+SSE (deprecated)

mcp.disconnect-done: The connection was removed and its tokens revoked.
mcp.issuer-changed: The server named another authorization server. Edit the server and confirm it.
mcp.connect-own-done: Your own account is connected; tests and syncs use it.
mcp.personal-connections-failed: The personal connections could not be counted.

server-editor.id-hint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, at most 40 characters. The id cannot change later.
server-editor.url-hint: https is required; http is only allowed for localhost during development.
server-editor.header-name-invalid: Use 1 to 128 letters, digits and dashes.
server-editor.user-name-hint: Sent with the secret as basic authentication.
server-editor.user-name-invalid: Enter a user name without a colon, at most 256 characters.
server-editor.secret-hint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
server-editor.secret-will-clear: The secret will be cleared when you save.
server-editor.secret-reference-hint: config:<name> reads NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Mcp:Secrets:<name> from the configuration; another prefix is a source the application registered, such as a vault. The secret is read for every connection, so a rotation applies at once.
server-editor.secret-reference-invalid: Enter a reference such as config:planning-token.
server-editor.client-certificate-hint: Optional. The name of a certificate that the application configured under NewHeap:AI:Assistant:Mcp:ClientCertificates, presented for mutual TLS.
server-editor.client-certificate-invalid: Use letters, digits, dots, underscores and dashes.
server-editor.transport-hint: Choose the fallback only for a server that does not offer Streamable HTTP yet.
server-editor.forward-warning: The signed-in user's token is sent to this server. The server's host must be on the allow-list of the application.

custom-auth.organization: The application supplies this credential; every caller shares it. It takes no secret here.
custom-auth.person: The application supplies each person's own credential. It takes no secret here.

server-editor.headless-use-hint: Agents that work without a person may use the tools with this server's own credential. The call still needs the rights of the person the agent works for, or, for an agent that acts for itself, a grant in the application code (mcp.<server id>.*).
server-editor.headless-use-personal: Background runs may use the server with a short-lived token of the person the run acts for, only after that person allowed it in their preferences.
server-editor.required-policy-hint: Optional. The server's tools are only available to users who pass this policy.
server-editor.connection-scope-hint: One connection makes everyone act as the organization's account. With personal connections every person connects their own account and the server sees who acts.
server-editor.oauth-warning: With one connection for everyone, every user of the server's agents acts as the connected account, with all its rights.
server-editor.registration-metadata-document: By the host's client metadata document
server-editor.registration-manual: A client id from the server's administrator is needed
server-editor.pkce-missing: This authorization server does not support PKCE with S256; it cannot be used.
server-editor.confirm-authorization: I confirm this authorization server for the server
server-editor.confirm-authorization-hint: Tokens are only requested from the confirmed authorization server. When the server names another one later, connections stop until you confirm again.
server-editor.confirm-required: Read the authorization and confirm it.
server-editor.scopes-hint: Space-separated. Only these scopes are requested; empty leaves the choice to the authorization server.
server-editor.scopes-invalid: Use scope names without quotes or backslashes, at most 1,024 characters.
server-editor.client-id-hint: Optional for authorization: without one the host registers itself when the server allows it. Required for client credentials.
server-editor.client-id-required: Enter the client id the authorization server issued.
server-editor.client-secret-hint: Stored encrypted and never shown again. Client credentials need a secret, a reference or the client certificate (private_key_jwt).
server-editor.organization-account-label-hint: Which account the organization connects, for example "Planning service account". Everyone using the server sees it.
server-editor.organization-account-label-required: Name the account that will be connected.

reader.title: Reading documents
reader.hint: Models that cannot read a file type themselves can get the file as text from a reader of this server. The assistant calls the reader's tool with the file name, media type and base64 content of the file, after the application's own readers.
reader.add-hint: Each reader is one of the server's synced tools; a server has at most {{max}}.
reader.limit: This server has the most readers it can have ({{max}}).
reader.media-types-invalid: Enter 1 to 16 media types of the form type/subtype, separated by commas.
reader.tool-hint: A tool synced from this server that turns a file into text. It does not have to be enabled for agents.
reader.tool-duplicate: Another reader of this server already uses this tool.
reader.tool-sync: Sync the server's tools first, then add a reader.
reader.priority-hint: Readers with a higher priority are asked first, after the application's own readers; with the same priority, by server and tool name.
reader.priority-invalid: Enter a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
reader.max-classification-hint: A file that is more sensitive is never sent to this server.
reader.leaves-application: A file sent to this server leaves the application. Choose a classification the server may receive; for personal connections the person's consent to background use still applies.

tools.title: Tools of {{name}}
tools.description: Tools stay disabled and are treated as changes that need approval until you enable them and choose the effect. Annotations from the server are hints only.
tools.empty: No tools yet. Sync the server to load its tools.
tools.schema-changed-warning: The tool's input changed on the server, so the tool was disabled. Review the tool before you enable it again.
tools.missing-warning: The server no longer lists this tool.

feedback.title: Feedback on proposals
feedback.description: What people said when they rejected this agent's proposals. Compare agent versions to see whether a change to the prompt, tools or policy helped.
feedback.export-hint: The export holds subject data and the proposed tool input, and is recorded in the audit log.
feedback.category-hint: The category narrows the feedback and the export.
feedback.summary-empty: The agent made no proposals in this period.
feedback.invalidated-hint: Open proposals that closed before anyone decided, because the work was already done or no longer applied. They do not count as rejected.
feedback.list-empty: Nobody gave feedback in this period.
feedback.author: By {{actor}}
feedback.bulk-hint: Given once for several proposals rejected together; weigh it lower.

evaluation.title: Evaluation of shadow variants
evaluation.description: Compares a shadow variant with the live agent: the runs that handled the same events, the proposals both made or only one made, what people decided about the live ones, and what each cost.
evaluation.export-hint: The export holds identifiers, statuses, usage and proposal identities, no messages or arguments. It is audited.
evaluation.small-numbers: Small numbers mislead: read the counts next to every share.
evaluation.replayed-hint: Replayed runs saw today's state of each subject; a subject that changed since can explain a difference.
evaluation.truncated: The period holds more runs than one evaluation reads; it covers the oldest ones.
evaluation.tools-empty: The paired runs made no proposals.
evaluation.replay-hint: Fires the live agent's recorded runs of the period into the variant, oldest first, against today's state of each subject; at most {{max}} runs. The variant's budget and limits apply.
evaluation.replay-progress: {{replayed}} of at most {{max}} runs replayed, {{skipped}} skipped

files.label: Accepts files
files.agent-hint: People's messages and the agent's tools may give it documents, such as PDFs, within the application's limits. A new agent accepts none until you switch this on.
files.skill-hint: Runs in this skill may read documents when the agent accepts them too. A new skill accepts none until you switch this on.
files.agent-limits-hint: Leave a field empty to keep the application's limit. A value can only lower it.
files.skill-limits-hint: Leave a field empty to keep the agent's limit. A value can only lower the application's.

run-config.title: Run configuration of {{name}}
run-config.description: Skills and triggers that the administration adds without a deploy, made of the building blocks the application registers. New skills and triggers start in shadow, where nobody is notified and nothing executes.

code.unknown-agent: the agent can no longer run on its own.
code.conflicts-with-code: the application now declares one with the same id.
code.too-many-skills: the agent has more skills than allowed.
code.tool-not-covered: a tool is outside the agent's own tools.
code.unknown-profile: the model profile no longer exists.
code.unknown-policy: the approval policy no longer exists.
code.unknown-filter: a filter of the event no longer exists, so the trigger starts nothing until you remove it.
code.unknown-subject-set: the set of subjects no longer exists.
code.invalid-schedule: the schedule or its time zone is not valid.
code.not-worked-on: it concerns a kind of object, or the whole application, that the agent does not work on.
code.unknown-subject-type: the kind of object no longer exists.
code.unknown-agent-policy: the policy the people who ask need is no longer listed.
code.conflicts-with-tool: another tool already has the name of its tool.
code.not-consultable: the application no longer lets administrators add consultations to this agent.
code.route-not-allowed: a route is no longer allowed, so it is left out.
code.agent-answers-to-person: the route with the agent's account is left out, because the agent answers to the object's responsible person.
code.agent-has-no-rights: the route with the agent's account is left out, because the agent answers for itself and has no rights of its own.
code.no-approver: the route with the agent's account is left out, because the approval policy lets only the person who caused a proposal decide it.
code.limit-above-ceiling: a limit is above what the application allows, so the application's applies.
code.requests-not-allowed: the application no longer allows requests, so it takes none.
code.mcp-not-allowed: the application no longer offers consultations to MCP clients, so they do not see it.
code.tools-not-allowed: a chosen tool is no longer among the agent's own tools, so it is left out; with none left the agent gets no tools in it.
code.no-asset-source: its instructions come from the application's text assets, which the application no longer offers.
code.asset-missing: the application no longer has the text asset with its instructions in this version.
code.asset-changed: the text of the asset with its instructions changed since it was saved, so it is not used. Read the asset again and save it as the next version.
code.asset-invalid: the application's text asset cannot be used as instructions.
code.asset-unavailable: the application's text assets could not be read; they are read again shortly.
code.outside-ceiling: the application no longer allows it.
code.unknown-source: an agent that may hand off can no longer run on its own.
code.unknown-live-agent: the agent this shadow variant follows can no longer run on its own.
code.live-agent-not-live: the agent this shadow variant follows is no live agent.
code.too-many-variants: the agent it follows has more shadow variants than the application allows.

field-errors.not-found: The application does not know this name.
field-errors.at-least: Enter a whole number of at least {{min}}.
field-errors.between: Enter a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
field-errors.budget-pair: Fill in both daily limits, or neither.
field-errors.dash-case: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter.
field-errors.taken: This id is already in use.
field-errors.name-letters: Use at least one letter in the name.
field-errors.instructions-for-model: Without fixed rules the model works from these instructions; describe what it should do.
field-errors.application-not-worked-on: The agent does not work on the whole application. Choose a set of objects, or let the agent work on the whole application first.
field-errors.megabytes-up-to: Enter a size above 0 and at most {{max}} MB.
field-errors.not-allowed: The application does not allow this.
field-errors.routes-required: Choose at least one route, or let it only answer.
field-errors.tools-not-allowed: A chosen tool is outside the agent's own tools. Clear it, or add the tool to the agent first.

settings.title: Run settings
settings.empty: This agent only chats. Let it work on its own: it then starts on events or a schedule, works by rules or with the model, and proposes changes that people approve.
settings.rights: It has no rights of its own: in runs without a person it uses what the account it answers to may use, within its tools.
settings.remove-explain: The agent then only chats. Remove its skills and triggers first.

accountability.subject-responsible: The person responsible for the subject

settings.accountability-hint: The agent acts with this account's rights. An agent that answers to itself has none and can only propose.
settings.triage-hint: A cheap model that chooses the skill of a run that no trigger or rule routed.

elevated.restricted: Shield from readers without the right

settings.gateway-reads: Read through the application's data gateway with the account's rights
settings.delegate: Also use what the person who starts a run may use

who.title: On whose behalf does the agent work?
who.explain: The agent has no rights of its own. In runs without a person it uses what this account may use, within its own tools.

accountability-explain.service-account: A technical account, for example an operations account. The usual choice.
accountability-explain.subject-responsible: The person responsible for the project or customer the run is about.
accountability-explain.agent: The agent itself: it has no rights and can only propose.

how.title: How does it work?
how.hint: Fixed rules decide without a model and hand doubtful cases to the model. This applies to runs that no skill handles.

approval.title: Who approves its proposals?
approval.hint: Proposals that change data wait for this approval; nothing executes before it.

settings.retries-hint: How often a failed run is tried again.
settings.max-concurrent-hint: Runs of this agent that work at the same time.
settings.max-per-subject-hint: Protects a project or customer from too many runs in one day.
settings.elevated-reads-hint: What happens when the agent reads data that the reader of its thread may not see.
settings.gateway-reads-hint: Lets the agent read through the application's data gateway, such as its API, as the account.
settings.delegate-hint: When a person starts a run by hand, the agent may also use that person's rights.

run-config.budget-hint: Leave empty for no limit. A daily budget needs both tool calls and tokens.
run-config.needs-settings: Give the agent run settings before you add skills and triggers.

skills.description: Skills in code come from the application. Skills added here have versions; a change goes live at once or runs in shadow next to the live version first.
skills.added: The skill is added. It starts in shadow; put it live from the agent's list.
skills.saved: The new version of the skill is live.
skills.saved-candidate: The new version runs in shadow next to the live version.
skills.removed: The skill is removed; its versions stay as history.
skills.empty: The agent has no skills yet.
skills.id-hint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, such as progress-note.
skills.description-hint: Triage and the model choose the skill by this description.
skills.instructions-hint: Read after the agent's own instructions while it works in the skill.
skills.tools-hint: The tools the agent offers; select some to narrow them for this skill. None selected: all of the agent's tools. Add tools to the agent with Edit.
skills.apply-shadow: Evaluate in shadow next to the live version first
skills.starts-in-shadow: A new skill starts in shadow.
skills.switch-on-now-hint: Otherwise the skill starts off: triggers that name it are ignored and rules and triage do not route to it until you switch it on in the agent list.
skills.remove-explain: Its versions stay as history. A trigger that starts it must go first.
skills.rules-hint: The rules decide without a model; a doubtful case goes to the model with the instructions below.
skills.model-hint: The model decides with the instructions below and the chosen tools.
skills.profile-hint: The model profile it uses; by default the agent's.

classification.label: Data classification
classification.hint: How sensitive the data is that the skill sends to its model. Its model profile must permit it; otherwise its model calls are refused.
classification.internal-hint: Data of the organization; the default.
classification.confidential-hint: Data only some people may see, such as personal or financial data.
classification.restricted-hint: The most sensitive data, for which only specially approved models may be used.

warnings.classification-not-permitted: Neither the skill's model profile nor the profile's fallbacks permit its data classification. The skill is saved, but its model calls are refused until a profile permits the classification.

skills.apply-shadow-hint: The new version runs next to the live one; compare them, then promote or discard it.
skills.apply-live-hint: For a small correction: the new version replaces the live one at once.
skills.background-hint: Started by a trigger the agent works without a chat: what it writes is kept with its run in the thread of what it works on, and changes become proposals.

candidate.explain: Version {{version}} runs in shadow next to the live version on the same events: {{description}}
candidate.promoted: The candidate is the live version now.
candidate.discarded: The candidate is discarded; it stays as history.
candidate.paired: Both handled {{count}} of the same events since {{date}}.

triggers.title: Triggers
triggers.description: Triggers in code come from the application. Triggers added here start the agent on the application's events or on a schedule.
triggers.added: The trigger is added. It starts in shadow.
triggers.empty: No triggers start the agent yet.
triggers.cron-hint: Five fields, such as 0 7 * * 1 for Mondays at seven.
triggers.starts-in-shadow: A new trigger starts in shadow.
triggers.id-hint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, for example project-created.
triggers.source-event-hint: Something happens in the application, such as a project being created.
triggers.source-schedule-hint: At fixed times, for every subject in a set.
triggers.source-schedule-application-hint: At fixed times, for the whole application or for every object in a set.
triggers.debounce-hint: Waits this long for more events about the same subject and handles them in one run.

filters.title: Filters
filters.hint: Skip events this trigger should not start the agent on, such as changes the agent made itself. Every filter you select must let an event through.
filters.missing: The event no longer offers this filter, so the trigger starts nothing. Clear it to save.

triggers.subject-set-hint: The projects or customers the schedule handles each time.
triggers.message-hint: What the agent reads as its task each time.

conflict-explain.coalesce: Adds the event to the waiting run.
conflict-explain.queue: Runs again after the busy run.
conflict-explain.supersede: Replaces the waiting run with this event.

target.title: What does it run for each time?
target.application-hint: One run each time, about the application as a whole.
target.application-per-division-hint: One run each time for every division, each in its own thread.
target.set-hint: One run each time for every object in a set, such as the active projects.
target.dropped: This schedule ran for the whole application, which the agent no longer works on. Choose a set of objects.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.explain: These options have sensible defaults; change them only when you need to.

account.search-placeholder: Search by name or e-mail address
account.search-hint: Choose the account by name or e-mail address. It must be able to sign in.
account.id-hint: The application offers no account search; enter the account's id. It must be able to sign in.
account.unknown: The application does not know this account.

mode.inline: The run waits for the decision.
mode.deferred: The run ends; people decide later.

policy-summary.four-eyes: Whoever caused the proposal may not approve it.

approver.named-role: someone with the role {{role}} on the subject

setup.start: Let this agent work on its own
setup.title: Let {{name}} work on its own
setup.explain: Four short questions. Everything starts in shadow: the agent works, but nobody is notified and nothing executes until you put it live.

what.title: What does it do?
what.name: Name of the task
what.name-hint: A short name, for example "Start new projects".

limits.title: Who approves, and what are its limits?

review.title: Review
review.schedule-application: On the schedule {{cron}} ({{zone}}), for the whole application
review.schedule-divisions: On the schedule {{cron}} ({{zone}}), for the whole application in every division
review.shadow: The task and its trigger start in shadow. Put them live now, or later from the run configuration.

setup.no-events: The application registers no events yet; choose a schedule.
setup.saved-shadow: The agent works in shadow now: it runs, but nobody is notified and nothing executes. Put the task and its trigger live when the results are right.

run-config.note-hint: Kept with this version in its history, with your name and the time. The agent does not read it.

flow.title: At a glance
flow.description: How the agent works, from what it works on to its results. Each step opens the form that changes it.
flow.problems: Some settings no longer fit the application and are out of effect. Each shows at its step below, with what fixes it.

works-on.undeclared: Its code does not say, so it works on all objects and not on the whole application.

target.code-set: For every object of a set in code
target.when-fired: For the object the event names

when.none: No trigger starts it: it runs only when someone runs it now.

scope.objects: Run now: for one of the objects it works on.
scope.application: Run now: for the whole application.
scope.application-and-objects: Run now: for the whole application or one of the objects it works on.
scope.division: Run now: for one division at a time.
scope.division-and-objects: Run now: for one division at a time or one of the objects it works on.

when.run-policy: For the whole application only by: {{policy}}.
when.paused: It is paused: a run started now waits until it is resumed.

run-now-unavailable.stopped: Run now: not while the agent is stopped.
run-now-unavailable.configured-off: Run now: not while the application's code switches the agent off.
run-now-unavailable.no-settings: Run now: only once the agent has run settings.
run-now-unavailable.no-catalog: Run now: not until the run catalog can be read.

when.no-consultations: No other assistant can consult it yet.

skills.code-rules: Fixed rules in the application's code
skills.none: No skills: every run works by its way of working and instructions.
skills.no-tools: No tools: it can only answer.
skills.places-at: A run's proposal waits at the object it names ({{type}}), where that object's approvers decide.
skills.places-in-run: A run's proposal waits in the run's own thread.
skills.tool-not-offered: {{selector}} is no longer offered: no tool of the application matches it.

headless.never: Not in runs on their own

use.unknown: Whether it is used in runs that start on their own is not known here.
use.never: Its tools are left out of runs that start on their own, such as trigger runs.
use.organization: Its tools are used in runs that start on their own, with the organization's credential.
use.organization-grant: Its tools are used in runs that start on their own with the organization's credential once the agent's code grants them, because the agent answers to itself.
use.personal: Its tools are used in runs that start on their own only with the consent of the person a run acts for.
use.personal-responsible: Its tools are used with the account of the person responsible for the object, once that person allows background use.
use.personal-initiator: Its tools are used only in runs a person started, with that person's account and consent.
use.personal-never-account: Its tools are not used: a technical account has no personal connection.
use.personal-never-agent: Its tools are not used: an agent that answers to itself has no personal connection.

warning.never: MCP server {{server}} is not used in runs that start on their own: its background use is off.
warning.personal-never-account: MCP server {{server}} is not used: it works with personal accounts and the agent answers to a technical account.
warning.personal-never-agent: MCP server {{server}} is not used: it works with personal accounts and the agent answers to itself.

account.no-settings: It has no run settings yet, so it cannot run on its own.

rights.agent: It has no rights of its own and can only propose.
rights.subject-responsible: Runs use what the person responsible for the object may use, within its tools.
rights.service-account: Runs use what this account may use, within its tools.
